clue.text: Bill a cleric? Exactly right

parts.note: AC is short for account, and a bill is an account to be settled
a curate is a junior clergyman, one example of a cleric

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a man called Bill is a clergyman, and is told yes, exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but stands for an account (AC); the question mark shows a curate is just one kind of cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means precise and correct, without error.

clue.text: It is the current fashion to tear round avoiding extremes

parts.note: the mode is whatever style is in vogue at present

indicators.note: round here means turned about, so the letters of tear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ripping things up is said to be the latest trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' reads as ripping, but under 'round' it is shuffled into a word for speed; 'It is' and 'to' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate describes something kept within reasonable limits, middle-of-the-road.

clue.text: See codes i.e. explained

indicators.note: explained suggests the letters are unravelled and set out afresh, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at some codes, which the abbreviation i.e. then explains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb telling you to look, but it is a noun: a bishop's see is his district.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the area under his authority, his diocese.

clue.text: Left without officer at bazaar worn out

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the officer's abbreviation is taken out of the word Left

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer
a fete is a fundraising fair, much like a bazaar

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned by the officer at a charity bazaar is left exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes LT from LEFT, leaving EF; a fete is a British summer fair with stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means exhausted and feeble, having lost its vigour.

clue.text: Girl at home in new role

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other
new signals that the letters of role are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A young woman settles comfortably into a new part at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' shuffles the part into ELOR, and the being-at-home word sits inside it; 'Girl' is the definition, as so often in older puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Elinor is a female first name, as in Elinor Dashwood of Sense and Sensibility.

clue.text: Station collapses in Africa

parts.note: Victoria is a major London railway station
falls means collapses, tumbles down

explanation.surface: A news line reporting that a railway station in Africa has fallen down.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is one of London's main railway terminals; the definition is the bare location, pointing to a landmark found in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfall on the Zambezi lies on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe, a famous African sight.

clue.text: One with a deceptively distant manner of speaking

definitions.text: One with a deceptively distant manner of speaking

parts.words: One with a deceptively distant manner of speaking
parts.note: describes a performer who throws the voice so it seems to come from elsewhere, such as a dummy

explanation.definitionFit: A ventriloquist makes speech appear to come from a puppet, not from their own lips.

clue.text: Roused by a bee perhaps

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the idiom literally: a bee sting gets anyone moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred into activity, as an idiom; literally, someone a bee has stung is jolted into moving.

clue.text: At home certain to take cover

parts.note: in means at home
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A homeowner, sure of themselves, takes out a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure is to buy protection, a policy guarding against loss.

clue.text: Neat gash has no dirt in it

definitions.text: gash has no dirt in it

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes a wound literally: a cut with no dirt is clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean-cut means tidy and wholesome in appearance; literally, a wound kept free of dirt is a clean cut.

clue.text: Port or whisky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the fortified wine, a drink like whisky; here it is the Sussex harbour town of Rye.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a small harbour town in East Sussex, England, and also a whiskey distilled from rye grain.

clue.text: Equip lady with a fleet of ships

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fit out a woman with a whole navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word joining the pieces; ADA is just a female name.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large naval force, most famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Directing the course of the cheapest accommodation

explanation.definitionFit: Steerage is the act of guiding a vessel, and also the lowest-priced passenger quarters on a ship.

clue.text: Being a bit tetchy-and the rest

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a fragment of it, so the answer lies within the letters of tetchy

explanation.surface: Someone is somewhat irritable, along with everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside tETChy; 'Being a bit' points to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc. abbreviates et cetera, Latin for the remaining things.

clue.text: Found in or under a railway carriage

definitions.text: Found in or under a railway carriage

parts.words: Found in or under a railway carriage
parts.note: two senses: a dozing passenger is in the carriage, and the wooden beam carrying the track lies under it

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sleeper is the beam under railway track (US: tie), as well as an overnight train coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a sleeping person, a sleeping-car, and a crosstie beneath the rails.

clue.text: Its contents will be very much alike

definitions.text: Its contents will be very much alike

parts.words: Its contents will be very much alike
parts.note: points to the idiom 'like two peas in a ...', a husk whose seeds look identical

explanation.definitionFit: A pea husk holds seeds so similar that they give the saying about identical people.

clue.text: Disturbance in court

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters of in court are scrambled

explanation.surface: A row breaks out in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: the letters of IN COURT are disturbed into an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy quarrel or row, the sort that might erupt in court.

clue.text: In fun be a tennis player not having suffered defeat

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Advice to enjoy yourself as a tennis player who never loses.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through fUN BE A TENnis; 'player' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbeaten describes a record with no losses.

clue.text: Cross right over a few lines

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the abbreviation for right is read backwards

parts.note: a verse is a few lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A poet crosses out a few lines of verse on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue means turned upside down, so the right abbreviation reads TR before the verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or over something.

clue.text: Detains eccentric as an alternative

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, signalling the letters of detains are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd character is held in custody in place of someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, as a substitute.

clue.text: Cavalry division form working party with Ronald

parts.note: a squad is a small team set to a task
Ron is the short form of Ronald

explanation.surface: A cavalry unit is told to set up a work team with a soldier called Ronald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' and 'with' are link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A squadron is a unit of cavalry, made up of troops.

clue.text: Crafty paintings almost complete

parts.note: paintings are works of art

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: full means complete, entire

explanation.surface: A cunning set of paintings is nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last L from FULL, giving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Artful means cunning and sly.

clue.text: Nothing more than an American farm hut

indicators.note: more than says the round letter for nothing is added on after the farm

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm in the US
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A humble US farm is described as no more than a shack.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage a rancho is a rough hut or group of huts for ranch hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancho in the US is a crude shelter, a shack for farm workers.

clue.text: Bachelor of Law goes to an ecclesiastical establishment to become pale

parts.note: BL is the abbreviation for Bachelor of Law, a degree
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A law graduate takes holy orders and turns white at the thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' is a link word placing the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To blanch is to turn white with fear or shock.

clue.text: Girl is confident without right

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for right is taken away from the word

parts.note: to be sure is to be confident

explanation.surface: A self-assured young woman is not correct after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes R from SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a woman's first name, short for Susan.

clue.text: Clearly seen to be separate

explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct means plainly visible and also individual, apart from others.

clue.text: A meal I cooked for a girl

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, signalling the letters of a meal I are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has prepared dinner for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia is a female first name.

clue.text: Made to learn the hard way presumably

definitions.text: Made to learn the hard way presumably

parts.words: Made to learn the hard way presumably
parts.note: describes someone shown through harsh experience what not to do, read also as a school lesson

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means punished so as to learn from a mistake.
